MAR.note: Only planned standards and guidelines for AI use in administration; no rule, draft or authority on AI harms.

facts.fact: Minister Ahmed Rahhou told the House of Representatives that his ministry is developing AI assistants, one to guide businesses through administrative procedures and a legal assistant for searching legislation and preparing draft laws and decrees, and plans pilot projects in other departments.

MAR.note: No AI tool in a sector's public system is stated.
Home-grown models, cloud and Jazari institutes are stated as plans or goals with no builder or site for a model, dataset or computing facility.
Digital identity adoption is only a stated priority.
Nothing on civil register and ID links.

facts.fact: Minister Rahhou said rural coverage in 2,000 areas in 2026 forms part of the second phase of the National Broadband and Ultra-Broadband Development Plan.
facts.system: National Broadband and Ultra-Broadband Development Plan

MAR.note: Nothing on e-procurement.
Nothing on the central bank.

facts.fact: Minister Rahhou said his ministry plans several rounds of digital and change-management training for officials through the Raed network, and to expand the Digital Academy platform for public administrations, with training for civil servants in AI pilot projects.

MAR.note: Nothing on digital finance consumer protection.
Nothing on cross-border payments.
Only a general aim of strengthening personal data protection; no law stated.

facts.fact: Minister Rahhou announced internet coverage will be activated in 2026 in 2,000 rural areas with poor or no access, under the second phase of the National Broadband and Ultra-Broadband Development Plan, with VSAT considered for hard-to-reach villages.
facts.system: National Broadband and Ultra-Broadband Development Plan, phase 2
